key_insight: Low-frequency bow-shock motion is governed by a spanwise mass-balance imbalance in the separated flow, especially the lag between inflow at reattachment and outflow through the horseshoe vortex core.
engineering_relevance: Understanding this mechanism helps predict and control shock-induced three-dimensional separation and associated unsteadiness on protuberances at supersonic speeds.
method: Wind tunnel experiments at Mach 2.87 with protuberances of different shapes and sizes
Time-resolved surface pressure measurements and schlieren imaging to quantify shock/separation dynamics
Compressible adaptive detached eddy simulation with POD and correlation analysis for a 15 mm cubic protuberance
evidence_signal: The study reports low-frequency shock oscillations at Stδ ~ 0.01 and mid-frequency separated-region pressure oscillations at Stδ ~ 0.1, supported by experiments and 3-D simulation modal analysis.
watch_item: The governing mechanism is inferred from one detailed simulated case, so broader generalization across all protuberance geometries and flow conditions should be treated cautiously.
paper_title: On the governing mechanism of unsteadiness in bow shock-induced three-dimensional separation
